title: Relative Timestamps in Log Configs
pattern: Configuring log outputs or diagnostic metrics to print elapsed relative durations instead of ISO 8601 absolute datetime stamps.
why_bad: Prevents temporal alignment during debugging. Operators cannot correlate application events to network issues or database outages on neighboring systems, rendering post-mortem analysis useless.
detection: The configuration or log formatter utilizes millisecond or microsecond relative execution offsets as its primary event identifier.
fix: Format all application logs using standardized timezone-aware absolute ISO 8601 timestamps, enabling clean temporal correlation across systems.
source: [Addison-Wesley Professional Computing Series] Richard L. Sites - *Understanding Software Dynamics* (2021, Addison-Wesley Professional).pdf, Section 8.5.
